binders: Universally quantify an arbitrary finite index type ι, with its finite enumeration, and a real square matrix A:ι×ι→ℝ.
Assume hcoefficient, asserting the existence of a real eigenvalue function and a real basis of ℝ^ι consisting of corresponding eigenvectors.
Universally quantify three arbitrary vectors L,O,R in ℝ^ι, representing the left state, the value at the spatial origin initially, and the right state.

After these inputs, existentially quantify λ:ι→ℝ and an indexed real basis e=(e_p)_{p∈ι} of ℝ^ι. These witnesses may depend on the preceding inputs, including L,O,R; the target does not place their existential quantifiers before the states.
For the eigenvector assertion quantify p∈ι; for the initial-value assertion quantify x∈ℝ; for the similarity assertion quantify x,t∈ℝ with t>0.
Within the conservation predicate, universally quantify real a,b,t for spatial integrability, real x,s,t for temporal flux integrability, and real a,b,s,t for the balance identity.
hypotheses: ι is finite; it is not required to be nonempty.
A is diagonalizable over ℝ in the explicit sense that there exist μ_p∈ℝ and a real basis (b_p)_{p∈ι} of ℝ^ι with Ab_p=μ_p b_p for every p.
There are no restrictions on L,O,R.
The self-similarity equality has the additional local hypothesis t>0; this hypothesis does not restrict the conservation or initial-value conclusions.
conclusions: There exist λ and e as above such that all the following assertions hold simultaneously.
For every real a,b,t, the function x↦q(x,t) is integrable on both (a,b] and (b,a] with respect to the designated real volume measure μ.
For every real x,s,t, the function τ↦Aq(x,τ) is integrable on both (s,t] and (t,s] with respect to μ.
For every real a,b,s,t, ∫_a^b q(x,t) dμ(x) − ∫_a^b q(x,s) dμ(x) = ∫_s^t [Aq(a,τ) − Aq(b,τ)] dμ(τ), with oriented vector-valued interval integrals.
For every real x, q(x,0)=L if x<0, q(x,0)=O if x=0, and q(x,0)=R if x>0.
For every real x and every real t>0, q(x,t)=q(x/t,1).
mathematical_definitions: The state space ℝ^ι consists of all functions ι→ℝ, with pointwise real vector operations and the supplied finite-product normed-space structure.
For a chosen basis e, write c_p(v) for the p-th basis coordinate of v, so v=Σ_{p∈ι} c_p(v)e_p. These coordinates come from eigenbasis.equivFun.
Define S(L,O,R;y)=L for y<0, O for y=0, and R for y>0; the same definition applies to scalar or vector values.
Define q:ℝ×ℝ→ℝ^ι by q(x,t)=Σ_{p∈ι} f_p(x−λ_p t)e_p. Equivalently, the coefficient of e_p is c_p(L) when x<λ_p t, c_p(O) when x=λ_p t, and c_p(R) when x>λ_p t.
The flux is the fixed linear map F(v)=Av.
Let μ be Real.measureSpace.volume. Define ∫_a^b g dμ = ∫_{(a,b]} g dμ − ∫_{(b,a]} g dμ. Interval integrability means integrability on both of these half-open sets.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite real square matrix admitting a real eigenbasis and every choice of left, origin, and right states, there exist real eigenvalues and a corresponding real basis such that the function obtained by translating each scalar basis-coordinate step profile at its eigenvalue and summing the resulting multiples of basis vectors has integrable spatial sections and integrable temporal flux sections on every bounded interval. For all real spatial and temporal endpoints it satisfies the exact conservation identity: the change in its spatial integral equals the time integral of flux at the left endpoint minus flux at the right endpoint. Its value at time zero is exactly the prescribed three-valued step function, including the separately prescribed value at the origin. At every positive time it satisfies q(x,t)=q(x/t,1). The function is defined for all real space and time by the displayed finite sum.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The matrix hypothesis requires a complete real eigenbasis. Merely having real eigenvalues is insufficient if the matrix is defective; no statement is made for matrices failing this hypothesis.
No distinctness, ordering, positivity, or nonzero condition is imposed on the eigenvalues. No symmetry of A or orthogonality or normalization of the basis is required.
If ι is empty, the state space has only its zero vector, all sums are empty, eigenvector assertions are vacuous, and the remaining equalities are trivial.
The conservation property includes all real times, including negative times and rectangles crossing time zero. Endpoints need not be ordered.
The similarity conclusion applies only to t>0, so it does not require division at zero and makes no corresponding assertion for negative time.
The value O is arbitrary and fixes each mode's value exactly on x=λ_p t. At such a line the full vector q need not equal O because other modes can be on different branches.
The target asserts a particular constructed function and its properties, but no uniqueness of that function, eigenvalues, or eigenbasis, and no independence from the choice of eigenbasis.

The conservation statement is an integral identity with explicit sectionwise integrability. It does not explicitly assert classical differentiability, a pointwise differential equation, a distributional test-function formulation, or entropy admissibility.
The initial condition is exact pointwise equality at time zero, not a separately asserted limit or trace as time tends to zero.
Only bounded-interval integrability is required; global integrability over the entire spatial or temporal real line is not required.
Integrability is explicitly required, so the balance is not asserted solely using potentially default values of integrals of nonintegrable functions.
ambiguities: D080 supplies Real.measureSpace only as inferInstance, without expanding the selected instance or its normalization. The exact translation therefore retains μ=Real.measureSpace.volume; identifying it independently as normalized Lebesgue measure cannot be verified from that body alone.
